Tukey’s test of multiple comparisons reduces the Type-I error of the family of pairwise tests. Which of the above statements are correct?
F16.2.explanation: All three: Scheffé covers every contrast via the 𝐹distribution; Tukey controls the familywise Type-I error (the 2018 Q11 key, with the false Bartlett statement removed).

F16.3.topic: Multiple Comparison Tests: Tukey, Scheffé, SNK, Duncan
F16.3.question: Among Scheffé, Tukey, Student–Newman–Keuls and Duncan, when applied to all pairwise comparisons, the most conservative procedure (widest critical differences) is generally
F16.3.explanation: For pairwise work Scheffé is widest (it pays for all contrasts); Duncan is the most liberal.

F16.4.topic: Multiple Comparison Tests: Tukey, Scheffé, SNK, Duncan
F16.4.question: In the Student–Newman–Keuls (SNK) procedure, the critical value used for comparing two ordered means depends on
options: only the total number of treatments 𝑘
the number of means spanned (the “stretch” 𝑝) between the two ordered means
only the error degrees of freedom
the value of the grand mean
F16.4.explanation: Stepwise range test: 𝑞𝛼;𝑝,𝜈with 𝑝the stretch of the two ordered means (2021 Q6 statement 2).

F16.5.topic: Multiple Comparison Tests: Tukey, Scheffé, SNK, Duncan

It uses protection level (1 −𝛼)𝑝−1 for a stretch of 𝑝means, so its critical values are smaller than those of SNK. II. It is more liberal (declares significance more readily) than Tukey’s HSD. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
F16.5.explanation: Duncan’s shrinking protection level makes it the high-power, low-protection member of the family.

F16.7.topic: Multiple Comparison Tests: Tukey, Scheffé, SNK, Duncan
F16.7.question: Consider the following statements: I. For simple pairwise differences, Tukey’s intervals are narrower than Scheffé’s. II. For complex contrasts involving several means, Scheffé’s method is the appropriate choice. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

If the overall 𝐹test is not significant, no contrast can be Scheffé-significant. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

F16.10.explanation: Equal 𝑛in the classical form; Tukey–Kramer handles unbalanced data.

F16.11.topic: Multiple Comparison Tests: Tukey, Scheffé, SNK, Duncan
